made: node docs/proyecto/pixel/cuarto-sheet-make.js, from cuarto-set.html (window.CUARTO.E) and the design of El cuarto (the orchestrator's p9-spec, general rules and section cuarto). A new scene: no old scene, no remap.

rules.project: pp-engine.js project(x, y, z) with S 26 and this origin: sx = OX + (x - y) / R2 * S, sy = OY + ((x + y) / R2 * .5 - z * COS) * S, depth d = (x + y) / R2 * COS + z * .5 (R2 = sqrt 2, COS = sqrt 3 / 2); OX = W / 2 + originX = 120, OY = H / 2 + originY = 66. A box is the screen bounding box of its projected corners [floor(min x), floor(min y), ceil(max x) - floor(min x), ceil(max y) - floor(min y)]. screen is the projection rounded to whole pixels
rules.uv: the set is laid out square to the picture: a spot is given in (u, v, z), u across the picture (to the right), v down it (towards the camera), the back wall at v 0; plaza-base.js PZ.xy(u, v) = ((u + v) / R2, (v - u) / R2) gives the world x, y (world is that). On the picture sx = OX + u * S = 120 + 26 u, and sy = OY + (v / 2 - z * COS) * S = 66 + 13 v - 22.5167 z; the picture holds u from -4.62 to 4.62. The beds are at u -1.5 and 1.2 (heads at v 0.25, feet at v 3.2, hw 0.66), the night table at u -0.15, the armchair at (-3.15, 1.3), the cradle at (2.28, 0.75), the chair at (2.9, 4.3)
rules.spot: a spot is a world point of the feet (z 0: the floor; z 0.44: a seat's top; z 0.5: a mattress's top; z 0.6: a pillow's top, the head's place; z 0.55: the night table's top) and, drawn there, a character stands with its feet (the lowest row the sprite draws, outline included) resting on the screen row sy, i.e. the sprite's bottom edge on sy, and its middle column on the column sx (rules.anchor). A small thing has a box (the spot's box): the bell, the plate, the big pillow, the clothes, the baby, the Z's and the nose have their bottom middle on the spot (the box [sx - floor(w / 2), sy - h, w, h]); the blanket on abuelo's knees is 8 px either side of the spot and from 6 px above it to 4 px below. scale is the frog's: 1 everywhere
rules.anchor: the column of the sprite that is on sx; its feet (its lowest drawn row, outline included) rest on row sy - 1, so its bottom edge is on sy. mkPersona (48 wide): column 24 (KIT.PX), 53 rows drawn standing for a grown-up (a 56-row canvas whose lowest row is empty), a child 43 rows; the frog mkCoqui(1) (32 x 27): column 16, drawn rows 1 to 24 (row 25 of the canvas is on sy); abuela standing mkAbuela (48 x 51): column 30 (her middle) and her bottom edge; a grown-up sitting (mkPersona with sent = 1): column 24 and the lap row, the bottom of the hips: row 16 + 2 t + 3 (t 11 a grown-up: 41; t 7 a child: 33) on (sx, sy); Canelo sitting (KIT.mkPerro, 30 x 22): the middle of his drawn columns and his bottom edge. WHOEVER LIES OR SITS UP IN A BED (cama_luis, cama_carmen): the standing sprite hangs DOWN the bed from the head's place: its highest drawn row (outline included: canvas row 2 for a child) and its middle column 24 on (sx, sy); only the rows from there down to the bed's foot are drawn (40 rows: the mattress's front face's bottom edge is row 100), and over them from his chest (sprite row 24, lying) or his waist (row 30, sitting up) to the foot a blanket of the bed's colour and the bed's width (34 px). Nobody is drawn turned
rules.view: one window, wide, zoom 1: the 196 x 216 window over the 240 x 216 picture, x0 = its left edge (22 centres it). Never a fraction
rules.depth: a spot's depth is the engine's d of its world point; front.plane turns it into the depth of each row of a character; front.hung is the rule for whoever lies in a bed

front.how: no list. A character is hidden by every set pixel that is nearer the camera than the character's feet (depth test against the baked depth, with the feet's depth plus 0.3): the armchair's seat hides the shins of whoever sits in it, the night table's front hides what stands behind it.
front.plane: for the character's pixel on picture row r (r = 0 at the top): depth(r) = d + (sy - (r + .5)) * tan(30 deg) / S, where d is the spot's depth and sy its screen row; the pixel is hidden where bakedZ[r * 240 + x] > depth(r) + bias (bakedZ: window.DEPTH.z of the set page). The same rule as El pedido's: the upright plane through the feet
front.hung: whoever lies or sits up in a bed (the spots with a hang): he lies on his mattress, so for his pixel on picture row r: depth(r) = (2 * COS / S) * (r + .5 - OY) + 2 * z0, with z0 = 0.5 (the mattress's top: the plane of a horizontal surface at that height), tested against the baked depth with the same bias. The upright rule would put the rows below his head BEHIND the mattress (they hang down the bed: nearer the camera, with a lower plane), and hide his body
front.sprites: between two sprites the nearer pixel wins: the same depth(r), no bias; two planes within 0.001 are a tie and the later layer is drawn

shadows.at: castShadow(x, y, 0, radius) at the world x, y of the spot, for a character standing on the floor (z 0). The spec gives no radius: these are El cruce's and El calendario's (open point)
shadows.onSeat: whoever lies in a bed, sits in the armchair, stands on the bed or on the chair (z above 0) casts none: none of those is floor (a shadow cast at the floor under them would show in front of them); the beds cast their own (CS.bed)
